Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// Declarative per-platform capability profiles (issue #1079, slice 1 —
+/// SDK foundation, additive).
+///
+/// A [HostCapabilityProfile] is the per-platform half of the capability ×
+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's
+/// ceiling — and every state is validated against it at construction.
+/// Violations throw [HostProfileViolation] loudly at build time (AC4), not
+/// at runtime.
+///
+/// Slice 1 ships the record types, the validation, the transport
+/// vocabularies and the seven built-in profiles (in `host_wiring_builder.dart`).
+/// No host migrates to them yet: hosts keep their hand-rolled wiring until
+/// the builder slices land.
+///
+/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`.

+
+import '../exceptions.dart';

+/// A host-wiring capability: one row of the issue #1079 capability ×
+/// platform matrix.
+///
+/// The set is closed on purpose (E2): adding a value breaks the
+/// matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it —
+/// "CLI got X, app didn't" dies at compile+construct time, not in a sweep.

+  configSections,
+
+  /// Compaction wiring: roles.smol judge, `overWindowRelief`,
+  /// `contextWindowCap`.
+  compaction,
+

+  loadModes,
+
+  /// MCP servers.
+  mcp,
+
+  /// Messaging fabric transports (file / hub / A2A).
+  messagingFabric,
+
+  /// Approval gate (modes, unattended, always-allow).
+  approvalGate,
+
+  /// Skills + project context.
+  skills,
+
+  /// Sandbox env (cube / platform / WasiSandbox / MemoryShell).
+  sandboxEnv,
+
+  /// Background shell jobs (the `bash_job` board).
+  backgroundShellJobs,
+
+  /// sqlite reader, `lsp`, `dap` tool families.
+  sqliteLspDap,
+
+  /// On-device providers (webllm / gemma in-process inference).
+  onDeviceProviders,
+
+  /// JS apps (jsr) + `dynamic_message` — the browser-API surface.
+  jsApps,
+
+  /// Checkpoint / rewind.
+  checkpointRewind,

+  hostExtensionApi,

+  subagents,

+  /// (`browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, …). Distinct from [jsApps]:
+  /// this is the automation surface the CLI wires today (fah.dart:2143).
+  /// Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven (AC10).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).

# pr-1091: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation

## Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// Declarative per-platform capability profiles (issue #1079, slice 1 —
+/// SDK foundation, additive).
+///
+/// A [HostCapabilityProfile] is the per-platform half of the capability ×
+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's
+/// ceiling — and every state is validated against it at construction.
+/// Violations throw [HostProfileViolation] loudly at build time (AC4), not
+/// at runtime.
+///
+/// Slice 1 ships the record types, the validation, the transport
+/// vocabularies and the seven built-in profiles (in `host_wiring_builder.dart`).
+/// No host migrates to them yet: hosts keep their hand-rolled wiring until
+/// the builder slices land.
+///
+/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`.

+
+import '../exceptions.dart';
+
+/// A host-wiring capability: one row of the issue #1079 capability ×
+/// platform matrix.
+///
+/// The set is closed on purpose (E2): adding a value breaks the
+/// matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it —
+/// "CLI got X, app didn't" dies at compile+construct time, not in a sweep.
+enum HostCapability {
+  /// `roles:`/`tools:`/`ttsr:`/`redact:`/`providerTimeouts:`/`agent:`
+  /// config sections.
+  configSections,
+
+  /// Compaction wiring: roles.smol judge, `overWindowRelief`,
+  /// `contextWindowCap`.
+  compaction,
+
+  /// Load modes + `discover_tools` demotion.
+  loadModes,
+
+  /// MCP servers.
+  mcp,
+
+  /// Messaging fabric transports (file / hub / A2A).
+  messagingFabric,
+
+  /// Approval gate (modes, unattended, always-allow).
+  approvalGate,
+
+  /// Skills + project context.
+  skills,
+
+  /// Sandbox env (cube / platform / WasiSandbox / MemoryShell).
+  sandboxEnv,
+
+  /// Background shell jobs (the `bash_job` board).
+  backgroundShellJobs,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

**Purity claims**: "no dart:io/dart:isolate imports in lib/src/hosts/" — verified true by reading; both files import only `../exceptions.dart` and each other.

**The double blank line in enum** — check `dart format`.

Let me also check `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` on the new files.

Also check line lengths (80 col convention). In `host_capability_profile.dart`:

```dart
typedef CapabilityTransports = ({Set<String> all, Set<String> defaults});
```
That's 81 chars? Let me count: "typedef CapabilityTransports = ({Set<String> all, Set<String> defaults});" = 74 chars. OK.

`const Map<HostCapability, CapabilityTransports> hostCapabilityTransports = {` — 77. OK.

In host_wiring_builder.dart:
`const CapabilitySurface({this.tokens = const {}, this.promptSectionIds = const {}});` — let me count: that's 86 chars — over 80. dart format would wrap it. So file is not formatted.

Also `/// [CapabilitySpec.requiredServices]` in a doc comment:
```dart
  /// Host-provided platform services, keyed by [CapabilitySpec
  /// .requiredServices] names (transport factories, stores, probes).
```
That's a broken doc reference — `[CapabilitySpec\n.requiredServices]` — dartdoc reference won't resolve. Minor.

Also `_requireServices`: `final absent = spec.requiredServices.difference(platformServices.keys.toSet());` — 83 chars, over 80.

Let me run dart format to check.

**Architectural review**:

- The design is coherent: sealed states, sealed floors, exhaustive switches. Good use of Dart 3 patterns.
- `HostCapabilityProfile` validation is solid: completeness, blank reasons, transport vocabulary, floor checks.
- One design concern: `CapabilityFloor.fromState` derives floor from state, meaning a profile is its own ceiling — documented. OK.

- **Type-safety of transports**: transports are raw `String`s, not an enum. A typo in a transport string (`'remtoe'`) is caught by the vocabulary check at construction. OK — though an enum per capability would be stronger; vocabulary map with strings is a pragmatic choice. Could flag as SUGGESTION.

- **`hostCapabilityTransports` map completeness**: `_validateState` does `hostCapabilityTransports[capability]!` — a null-assertion. If a new enum value is added without a vocabulary entry, this throws a runtime TypeError/StateError rather than a HostProfileViolation. The enum comment says "adding a value breaks the matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it" — but the failure would be an unhandled null-check crash in validation, not a nice violation message. Actually wait: `_requireComplete` catches missing states first; but the vocabulary map — if the new capability has no vocabulary entry, then in `_validateState`, `hostCapabilityTransports[capability]!` throws only if state is transport (accessed inside `if state is CapabilityTransportState`) OR in floor validation for `FloorTransports` with `on` state (defaults access) OR in builder (`hostCapabilityTransports[capability]!.defaults` for on states). A plain `on` state with `FloorOn` never touches the map... Actually in `build()`: `case CapabilityOnState(): _requireServices(...); entries.add(WiredCapability(capability, hostCapabilityTransports[capability]!.defaults));` — crash. And in the catalog: `hostCapabilityCatalog[capability]!` in `surfacedTokens`... The matrix-completeness TEST would catch missing catalog entries ("the catalog covers every capability in the enum" test). And a missing vocabulary entry would crash with a raw null-check error instead of HostProfileViolation — the E2 guard would be nicer if it validated vocabulary completeness too. SUGGESTION.

- **`CapabilitySpec` mutable?** All final. Good.

- **`HostWiringPlan.entries` ordering** — deterministic (HostCapability.values order). Good.

- **Test helper `cliPlatformServices` in test file** — fine.

- **`platformServices` typed `Map<String, Object>`** — values typed Object, no type safety on service types (can pass `Object()` as hubFabric). For slice 1 skeleton acceptable; slice 2 will need typed services. SUGGESTION.

- **The catalog claims `webSearch` requires `webSearchSecrets`** — but cliProfile wires `webSearch: on`, so building the CLI plan REQUIRES `webSearchSecrets` service. In the real CLI, `WebSearchConfig(secrets: webSearch)` — matches.

- **Missing `platformServices` for `visionTranscribe`/`subagents`** as noted.

- **`cliHelpText` AC7 test design flaw** — the BLOCKING one. Note also the helper `expectTextFreeOf` does substring matching: token `jsr` also matches `jsr.ext` etc. The test asserts help text doesn't contain 'jsr' — but help legitimately documents `fa jsr` pass-through (a *wired* capability — the QuickJS extension/widget tooling). The catalog's `jsApps` surface claims the `jsr` token, and `jsExtensions` claims `js_ext` + `jsr.ext`. So token ownership is wrong or ambiguous: `jsr` as a substring appears for the jsr widget pass-through. Actually, hmm — is the `fa jsr` pass-through part of `jsApps`? The matrix row jsApps says "JS apps (jsr) + dynamic_message — the browser-API surface". The `fa jsr widget:test` pass-through runs widget tests via the jsr agent CLI (a Node-based CLI?) — that's arguably the same "jsr apps" surface executed via CLI delegation rather than browser APIs! Interesting: the catalog pins jsApps OFF on the CLI with reason "no browser APIs on the Dart VM; jsr apps and dynamic_message need a JS host". But the CLI *does* wire `fa jsr widget:test` (delegating to the jsr CLI which uses its own JS host). So either:
  (a) the `fa jsr` pass-through is a separate capability not covered by any catalog row (an AC10 inventory miss!), or
  (b) it IS the jsApps row, in which case the CLI's today-state for jsApps is not honestly `off` — the CLI delegates to the jsr CLI, so the CLI does surface jsr.

  Either way, the PR's own AC10 claim "catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability" is violated by the `fa jsr widget:test/widget:screenshot` pass-through (merged via #1062): it's a CLI-wired capability absent from the catalog. This is a strong, evidence-backed finding. The failing test is the canary.

Let me check what `fa jsr` does to characterize it correctly.

Also check `dynamic_message` in the codebase to see what it is.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass.
