# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

blocks.text:
So the `jsr` pass-through was merged into main (#1062), and this PR branch merged main in commit 850e525d1, bringing the `jsr` help text in. The author then re-ran tests... or maybe not. The test now fails because:

1. The `jsApps` capability surface tokens are `{'jsr', 'dynamic_message'}`.
2. The real CLI help legitimately contains `jsr` — as the pass-through delegate for the widget-test CLI (a distinct feature, arguably closest to `jsExtensions`, which is *wired* on the CLI).

The failure is a genuine design flaw in the raw-text absence check: substring matching on short ambiguous tokens (`jsr`) produces false positives when the same string belongs to another, wired capability's surface. The fix is either:
- Disambiguate tokens (e.g. use `/jsr apps` or distinctive tokens), or
- Attribute the `jsr` help section to the right capability (jsExtensions?) — but note `jsExtensions` surface tokens are `{'js_ext', 'jsr.ext'}`, weird tokens, and `jsr.ext` is a weird token (with a dot). Actually `jsr.ext` — hmm.

Also interesting: the PR description explicitly claims "27/27 tests pass (`dart test/hosts/`)" and "the real cliHelpText carries zero jsr/dynamic_message references" — that claim is now false after the main merge. That's a BLOCKING CI issue (the test suite is red).

Note the PR says "CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it" — so the author didn't run CI; the branch is red and the PR description's evidence table is stale/wrong.

Let me also double-check the count of tests: "27 tests" claimed; actual run: 26 passed + 1 failed = 27 total. OK.

Now let me run a broader analysis to look for other issues. Let me check:

1. `dart analyze` on whole repo? Not needed; the changed files are clean.
2. Test the purity claim: no dart:io imports in lib/src/hosts/. The test file imports `dart:io` (fine, it's a test).
3. Look at the naming/structure conventions of the codebase: how other libs are structured, whether enums with switch-based `id` getters match conventions, etc.

Let me also review deeper issues:

**In host_capability_profile.dart:**

1. `HostCapability` enum `id` getter — uses switch expression; fine, but a double space after `jsExtensions;` before the doc comment `/// Stable catalog id`. Minor formatting: there's an extra blank line (two blank lines) between the enum values and the `id` getter. Actually looking at the code:

```dart
  jsExtensions;


  /// Stable catalog id (snake_case, matches the matrix row).
  String get id => switch (this) {
```

There are two blank lines after `jsExtensions;` — dart format would collapse this? Actually `dart format` preserves at most one blank line. So the file is NOT formatted with `dart format` (which is likely enforced by CI or conventional in the repo). Let me check formatting with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none`.

2. In `_validateState`, the message for unknown transports: `'${unknown.isEmpty ? state.transports : unknown}'` — when transports is empty (isEmpty case), it prints `state.transports` which is empty set `{}`. OK-ish. But message reads "unknown transports {} — valid: [...]" which is a bit confusing for the empty case. Minor.

3. `CapabilityState.transport` static method — the constructor `CapabilityTransportState(transports, reason)` — fine.

4. In `HostCapabilityProfile.narrowed`, the merged map uses `Map.of(states)..addAll(overrides)` then `_validate(name: label, states: merged, floors: floors)` and `HostCapabilityProfile._(label, Map.unmodifiable(merged), floors)`. Wait — floors passed to the private constructor is the same map instance as `this.floors`. That's fine since both are unmodifiable.

However, there's a subtle design flaw: `narrowed` does NOT complete the floor table from the new merged states — it keeps the base floors fixed (which is intended per docs). But what if the base profile derived floors from its own states (profile = its own ceiling)? E.g., `narrowed()` on a built-in profile whose floors were derived: the floor table for capabilities not explicitly floored = derived from the ORIGINAL state. So if the original state was `off` and you `narrowed` to `on`, validation checks against `FloorOff` → throws. That's the "profile is its own ceiling" semantics — intended.

But there's a subtle bug: `FloorOff(reason)` from a derived floor — the floor's reason is the ORIGINAL profile's off reason. If you narrow `jsApps: off("x")` on cli (floor derived FloorOff("no browser APIs on the Dart VM...")), fine.

Another subtlety: in `narrowed`, the merged states get validated against the FIXED floor table. But for capabilities whose floors were DERIVED from base states, narrowing a capability to a state whose envelope differs from the base (e.g., base was `transport({'remote'})` → floor `FloorTransports({'remote'})`; narrow to `transport({'remote'})` with different reason) — allowed. Narrow UP to `on` — rejected since defaults {stdio, remote} ⊄ {'remote'}. OK, consistent with "narrow-only".

BUT: the test `macOS may explicitly narrow UP to stdio` works because macos explicitly declares `floors: {mcp: FloorTransports({'stdio', 'remote'})}`. Fine.

5. `CapabilityFloor.fromState(CapabilityOnState() ) => const FloorOn()` — derived floors mean a profile's `on` state allows any state to be narrowed... fine.

6. The `states` map passed to the factory — `Map.unmodifiable(states)` wraps but doesn't deep-copy; callers can mutate their original map afterward? No — unmodifiable view prevents mutation through the view but the underlying map is still owned by caller... `Map.unmodifiable` creates a new map? Let me recall: `Map.unmodifiable(other)` creates a new UnmodifiableMapView... Actually `Map.unmodifiable(mapData)` returns `UnmodifiableMapView(Map.of(mapData))`? Let me check the SDK: 

```dart
factory Map.unmodifiable(Map<dynamic, dynamic> other) {
  final result = <dynamic, dynamic>{};
  other.forEach((k, v) { result[k as K] = v as V; });
  return UnmodifiableMapView(result);
}
```

Yes — `Map.unmodifiable` COPIES entries into a new map, then wraps in an unmodifiable view. So the copy is safe. Good.

7. `HostWiringPlan.planFor` uses `firstWhere` without `orElse` — throws StateError for unknown capability. Since entries are complete over the catalog (built from HostCapability.values), fine — but if called with a capability not in `HostCapability.values`... can't happen (typed enum). OK.

8. `surfacedTokens` — builds transport-qualified tokens as `'${entry.capability.id}:$t'` — e.g. `mcp:stdio`. And the AC7 hiding helper checks `plan.surfacedTokens` isNot contains `${capability.id}:$t`. Consistent.

9. In `CapabilitySurface` constructor formatting: `const CapabilitySurface({this.tokens = const {}, this.promptSectionIds = const {}});` — line length. The repo probably enforces 80-col formatting via dart format. Let me check.

**In host_wiring_builder.dart:**

10. `hostCapabilityCatalog` — top-level `final Map ... Map.unmodifiable({...})` — eager init. Fine.

11. `CapabilitySpec` — `requiredServices` for capabilities that need services. Note `onDeviceProviders` and `jsApps` have no `requiredServices` — but they're off in CLI. If a custom host turns `onDeviceProviders` on and builds, the builder requires NO services — silently wiring nothing. Hmm — but the builder only returns a plan (description); services matter in slice 2. Still, an `on` for `onDeviceProviders` with empty `requiredServices` produces a `WiredCapability` without any service — the plan says "wired" but no factory exists. This is an E1 gap: inventory-driven rows have `requiredServices` for some (`webSearchSecrets`, `browserBridgeHandle`, `extRuntimeFactory`) but `visionTranscribe` and `subagents` have NONE. If a host wires `subagents: on` without any service, the plan says wired. Since subagents need SubagentManager config, that's a latent gap — but acceptable for slice 1 skeleton? The E1 contract says "a missing service fails at build, named" — for capabilities with no declared services, nothing to fail. It's a known gap worth flagging as SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT: `visionTranscribe` and `subagents` (and `onDeviceProviders`, `jsApps`) declare no required services, so E1 cannot catch a host that forgets their bac…

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.

# pr-1091: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation

## Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

blocks.text:
Fix #4 confirmed: `expectTextFreeOf` now uses `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])TOKEN(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` boundary matching.

Wait — there's a subtle BUG potential in this regex: the trailing lookahead is actually a consuming character class `[^A-Za-z0-9_]`, not a lookahead. Two consequences:

1. **Adjacent-token misses (false negatives)**: if two occurrences overlap sharing a delimiter, e.g. text "task task" — first match consumes "task " (including the trailing space), and the second "task" starts right after — `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` before it is the space — consumed by previous match? No — regex hasMatch finds the FIRST match anywhere; for ABSENCE checking we only need to know if ANY occurrence exists. Overlapping-consumption only matters with overlapping occurrences like "task"? Not a real concern for hasMatch absence.

   But a REAL false-negative case: two tokens adjacent like "task,lsp" — irrelevant, absence checks are per-token.

   More relevant false-negative: token at text edge handled via `(?:^|...)`. OK.

2. **`dynamic_message` token check on cliHelpText**: pattern `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])dynamic_message(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — help text has no dynamic_message. OK.

3. Escaping: `RegExp.escape(token)` escapes special chars; `\$` inside a single-quoted Dart string with `(?:\$|...)` — that's a literal `$` alternation for end-of-text anchor... wait: `(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — `\$` in the regex is an escaped literal dollar sign? NO — in Dart source `'(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])'` the `\$` produces the string `$` which in REGEX means end-of-input anchor. So the regex is `(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — correct: end of text or non-identifier char. Good.

   Similarly `^` anchors start-of-line (RegExp default is not multiline — `^` = start of text unless multiLine:true; hasMatch scans — `^` matches only at text start without multiLine). Hmm: `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — fine: start-of-text or non-word char.

   One subtlety: without multiLine, `^` matches only at position 0 — good for whole-text.

   But there's an edge: a token occurring at the START of a LINE (not position 0) preceded by '\n' — '\n' is a non-identifier char → matches via [^A-Za-z0-9_]. Good.

4. Now the semantics test: `expectTextFreeOf('boundary probe', {'task', 'lsp'}, 'run the tasks via help')` — pattern for 'task': `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])task(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — 'tasks' — 'task' followed by 's' (word char) → no match. Passes (no throw). 'use task here' — ' task ' → match → expect(false) → TestFailure. Correct.

   BUT: 'lsp' inside 'help' — 'help' contains 'lsp'? h-e-l-p. No 'lsp' substring ('lp' yes, 'lsp' no). Whatever — the test passes as written ('tasks' has no 'task'+boundary, 'help' has no 'lsp').

5. Doc comment nit: "Tokens match on identifier boundaries... `jsr` must not 'leak' inside `jsr.ext`'s owner or a longer identifier" — prose slightly odd but fine.

Now — new subtle issue with the boundary matcher and the token `'roles:'` (configSections) or `'mcp:'`: `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])mcp:(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — 'mcp:' in text 'the mcp: config' — ':' after 'mcp', then needs non-ident after ':' — ' config' → space. Match. Fine. These are wired for CLI so absence isn't checked against CLI help anyway.

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// Declarative per-platform capability profiles (issue #1079, slice 1 —
+/// SDK foundation, additive).
+///
+/// A [HostCapabilityProfile] is the per-platform half of the capability ×
+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's
+/// ceiling — and every state is validated against it at construction.
+/// Violations throw [HostProfileViolation] loudly at build time (AC4), not
+/// at runtime.
+///
+/// Slice 1 ships the record types, the validation, the transport
+/// vocabularies and the seven built-in profiles (in `host_wiring_builder.dart`).
+/// No host migrates to them yet: hosts keep their hand-rolled wiring until
+/// the builder slices land.
+///
+/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`.

+
+import '../exceptions.dart';

+/// A host-wiring capability: one row of the issue #1079 capability ×
+/// platform matrix.
+///

+/// matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it —
+/// "CLI got X, app didn't" dies at compile+construct time, not in a sweep.

+  /// config sections.
+  configSections,
+
+  /// Compaction wiring: roles.smol judge, `overWindowRelief`,
+  /// `contextWindowCap`.
+  compaction,
+

+  loadModes,

+  mcp,

+  messagingFabric,
+

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

# pr-1091: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation

## Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). blocks.text:
Fix #4 confirmed: `expectTextFreeOf` now uses `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])TOKEN(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` boundary matching.

Wait — there's a subtle BUG potential in this regex: the trailing lookahead is actually a consuming character class `[^A-Za-z0-9_]`, not a lookahead. Two consequences:

1. **Adjacent-token misses (false negatives)**: if two occurrences overlap sharing a delimiter, e.g. text "task task" — first match consumes "task " (including the trailing space), and the second "task" starts right after — `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` before it is the space — consumed by previous match? No — regex hasMatch finds the FIRST match anywhere; for ABSENCE checking we only need to know if ANY occurrence exists. Overlapping-consumption only matters with overlapping occurrences like "task"? Not a real concern for hasMatch absence.

   But a REAL false-negative case: two tokens adjacent like "task,lsp" — irrelevant, absence checks are per-token.

   More relevant false-negative: token at text edge handled via `(?:^|...)`. OK.

2. **`dynamic_message` token check on cliHelpText**: pattern `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])dynamic_message(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — help text has no dynamic_message. OK.

3. Escaping: `RegExp.escape(token)` escapes special chars; `\$` inside a single-quoted Dart string with `(?:\$|...)` — that's a literal `$` alternation for end-of-text anchor... wait: `(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — `\$` in the regex is an escaped literal dollar sign? NO — in Dart source `'(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])'` the `\$` produces the string `$` which in REGEX means end-of-input anchor. So the regex is `(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — correct: end of text or non-identifier char. Good.

   Similarly `^` anchors start-of-line (RegExp default is not multiline — `^` = start of text unless multiLine:true; hasMatch scans — `^` matches only at text start without multiLine). Hmm: `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — fine: start-of-text or non-word char.

   One subtlety: without multiLine, `^` matches only at position 0 — good for whole-text.

   But there's an edge: a token occurring at the START of a LINE (not position 0) preceded by '\n' — '\n' is a non-identifier char → matches via [^A-Za-z0-9_]. Good.

4. Now the semantics test: `expectTextFreeOf('boundary probe', {'task', 'lsp'}, 'run the tasks via help')` — pattern for 'task': `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])task(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — 'tasks' — 'task' followed by 's' (word char) → no match. Passes (no throw). 'use task here' — ' task ' → match → expect(false) → TestFailure. Correct.

   BUT: 'lsp' inside 'help' — 'help' contains 'lsp'? h-e-l-p. No 'lsp' substring ('lp' yes, 'lsp' no). Whatever — the test passes as written ('tasks' has no 'task'+boundary, 'help' has no 'lsp').

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// Declarative per-platform capability profiles (issue #1079, slice 1 —
+/// SDK foundation, additive).
+///
+/// A [HostCapabilityProfile] is the per-platform half of the capability ×
+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's
+/// ceiling — and every state is validated against it at construction.
+/// Violations throw [HostProfileViolation] loudly at build time (AC4), not
+/// at runtime.
+///
+/// Slice 1 ships the record types, the validation, the transport
+/// vocabularies and the seven built-in profiles (in `host_wiring_builder.dart`).
+/// No host migrates to them yet: hosts keep their hand-rolled wiring until
+/// the builder slices land.
+///
+/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`.

+
+import '../exceptions.dart';
+
+/// A host-wiring capability: one row of the issue #1079 capability ×
+/// platform matrix.
+///
+/// The set is closed on purpose (E2): adding a value breaks the
+/// matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it —
+/// "CLI got X, app didn't" dies at compile+construct time, not in a sweep.

+  /// `roles:`/`tools:`/`ttsr:`/`redact:`/`providerTimeouts:`/`agent:`
+  /// config sections.
+  configSections,
+
+  /// Compaction wiring: roles.smol judge, `overWindowRelief`,
+  /// `contextWindowCap`.
+  compaction,
+
+  /// Load modes + `discover_tools` demotion.
+  loadModes,
+
+  /// MCP servers.
+  mcp,
+
+  /// Messaging fabric transports (file / hub / A2A).
+  messagingFabric,
+
+  /// Approval gate (modes, unattended, always-allow).
+  approvalGate,
+
+  /// Skills + project context.
+  skills,
+
+  /// Sandbox env (cube / platform / WasiSandbox / MemoryShell).
+  sandboxEnv,
+
+  /// Background shell jobs (the `bash_job` board).
+  backgroundShellJobs,
+
+  /// sqlite reader, `lsp`, `dap` tool families.
+  sqliteLspDap,
+
+  /// On-device providers (webllm / gemma in-process inference).
+  onDeviceProviders,
+
+  /// JS apps (jsr) + `dynamic_message` — the browser-API surface.
+  jsApps,
+
+  /// Checkpoint / rewind.
+  checkpointRewind,
+
+  /// Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections /
+  /// bridges through the builder. Core behaviors stay SDK-invariant.
+  hostExtensionApi,

+  /// `web_search`/`web_fetch` tools over the `WebSearchConfig` secrets.
+  /// Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven (AC10): the CLI wires it
+  /// (fah.dart:2114) and no matrix row covers it.

+  /// generation over the host `visionConfig`/`transcribeConfig`.
+  /// Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven (AC10, fah.dart:2112-2113).

+  /// `task*`/`agent_*` tools. Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven
+  /// (AC10, agent_cli.dart:481-605).
+  subagents,
+
+  /// The browser tool family over the loopback bridge handle
+  /// (`browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, …). Distinct from [jsApps]:
+  /// this is the automation surface the CLI wires today (fah.dart:2143).
+  /// Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven (AC10).
+  browserBridge,

+  /// The QuickJS extension host (`extRuntimeFactory`, `initJsExtensions`,
+  /// `jsr_runtime`) — the CLI's process-based JS extension mechanism.

messages.preview: The suite is red: **1 of 27 tests fails** despite the PR claiming 27/27 green. Let me investigate the failure root cause and check related surfaces.

blocks.text:
So the `jsr` pass-through was merged into main (#1062), and this PR branch merged main in commit 850e525d1, bringing the `jsr` help text in. The author then re-ran tests... or maybe not. The test now fails because:

1. The `jsApps` capability surface tokens are `{'jsr', 'dynamic_message'}`.
2. The real CLI help legitimately contains `jsr` — as the pass-through delegate for the widget-test CLI (a distinct feature, arguably closest to `jsExtensions`, which is *wired* on the CLI).

The failure is a genuine design flaw in the raw-text absence check: substring matching on short ambiguous tokens (`jsr`) produces false positives when the same string belongs to another, wired capability's surface. The fix is either:
- Disambiguate tokens (e.g. use `/jsr apps` or distinctive tokens), or
- Attribute the `jsr` help section to the right capability (jsExtensions?) — but note `jsExtensions` surface tokens are `{'js_ext', 'jsr.ext'}`, weird tokens, and `jsr.ext` is a weird token (with a dot). Actually `jsr.ext` — hmm.

Also interesting: the PR description explicitly claims "27/27 tests pass (`dart test/hosts/`)" and "the real cliHelpText carries zero jsr/dynamic_message references" — that claim is now false after the main merge. That's a BLOCKING CI issue (the test suite is red).

Note the PR says "CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it" — so the author didn't run CI; the branch is red and the PR description's evidence table is stale/wrong.

Let me also double-check the count of tests: "27 tests" claimed; actual run: 26 passed + 1 failed = 27 total. OK.

Now let me run a broader analysis to look for other issues. Let me check:

1. `dart analyze` on whole repo? Not needed; the changed files are clean.
2. Test the purity claim: no dart:io imports in lib/src/hosts/. The test file imports `dart:io` (fine, it's a test).
3. Look at the naming/structure conventions of the codebase: how other libs are structured, whether enums with switch-based `id` getters match conventions, etc.

Let me also review deeper issues:

**In host_capability_profile.dart:**

1. `HostCapability` enum `id` getter — uses switch expression; fine, but a double space after `jsExtensions;` before the doc comment `/// Stable catalog id`. Minor formatting: there's an extra blank line (two blank lines) between the enum values and the `id` getter. Actually looking at the code:

```dart
  jsExtensions;


  /// Stable catalog id (snake_case, matches the matrix row).
  String get id => switch (this) {
```

There are two blank lines after `jsExtensions;` — dart format would collapse this? Actually `dart format` preserves at most one blank line. So the file is NOT formatted with `dart format` (which is likely enforced by CI or conventional in the repo). Let me check formatting with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none`.

2. In `_validateState`, the message for unknown transports: `'${unknown.isEmpty ? state.transports : unknown}'` — when transports is empty (isEmpty case), it prints `state.transports` which is empty set `{}`. OK-ish. But message reads "unknown transports {} — valid: [...]" which is a bit confusing for the empty case. Minor.

3. `CapabilityState.transport` static method — the constructor `CapabilityTransportState(transports, reason)` — fine.

4. In `HostCapabilityProfile.narrowed`, the merged map uses `Map.of(states)..addAll(overrides)` then `_validate(name: label, states: merged, floors: floors)` and `HostCapabilityProfile._(label, Map.unmodifiable(merged), floors)`. Wait — floors passed to the private constructor is the same map instance as `this.floors`. That's fine since both are unmodifiable.

However, there's a subtle design flaw: `narrowed` does NOT complete the floor table from the new merged states — it keeps the base floors fixed (which is intended per docs). But what if the base profile derived floors from its own states (profile = its own ceiling)? E.g., `narrowed()` on a built-in profile whose floors were derived: the floor table for capabilities not explicitly floored = derived from the ORIGINAL state. So if the original state was `off` and you `narrowed` to `on`, validation checks against `FloorOff` → throws. That's the "profile is its own ceiling" semantics — intended.

But there's a subtle bug: `FloorOff(reason)` from a derived floor — the floor's reason is the ORIGINAL profile's off reason. If you narrow `jsApps: off("x")` on cli (floor derived FloorOff("no browser APIs on the Dart VM...")), fine.

Another subtlety: in `narrowed`, the merged states get validated against the FIXED floor table. But for capabilities whose floors were DERIVED from base states, narrowing a capability to a state whose envelope differs from the base (e.g., base was `transport({'remote'})` → floor `FloorTransports({'remote'})`; narrow to `transport({'remote'})` with different reason) — allowed. Narrow UP to `on` — rejected since defaults {stdio, remote} ⊄ {'remote'}. OK, consistent with "narrow-only".

Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —

+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;

+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the

# pr-1091: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation

## Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

Fix #4 confirmed: `expectTextFreeOf` now uses `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])TOKEN(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` boundary matching.

Wait — there's a subtle BUG potential in this regex: the trailing lookahead is actually a consuming character class `[^A-Za-z0-9_]`, not a lookahead. Two consequences:

1. **Adjacent-token misses (false negatives)**: if two occurrences overlap sharing a delimiter, e.g. text "task task" — first match consumes "task " (including the trailing space), and the second "task" starts right after — `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` before it is the space — consumed by previous match? No — regex hasMatch finds the FIRST match anywhere; for ABSENCE checking we only need to know if ANY occurrence exists. Overlapping-consumption only matters with overlapping occurrences like "task"? Not a real concern for hasMatch absence.

   But a REAL false-negative case: two tokens adjacent like "task,lsp" — irrelevant, absence checks are per-token.

   More relevant false-negative: token at text edge handled via `(?:^|...)`. OK.

2. **`dynamic_message` token check on cliHelpText**: pattern `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])dynamic_message(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — help text has no dynamic_message. OK.

3. Escaping: `RegExp.escape(token)` escapes special chars; `\$` inside a single-quoted Dart string with `(?:\$|...)` — that's a literal `$` alternation for end-of-text anchor... wait: `(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — `\$` in the regex is an escaped literal dollar sign? NO — in Dart source `'(?:\$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])'` the `\$` produces the string `$` which in REGEX means end-of-input anchor. So the regex is `(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — correct: end of text or non-identifier char. Good.

   Similarly `^` anchors start-of-line (RegExp default is not multiline — `^` = start of text unless multiLine:true; hasMatch scans — `^` matches only at text start without multiLine). Hmm: `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — fine: start-of-text or non-word char.

   One subtlety: without multiLine, `^` matches only at position 0 — good for whole-text.

   But there's an edge: a token occurring at the START of a LINE (not position 0) preceded by '\n' — '\n' is a non-identifier char → matches via [^A-Za-z0-9_]. Good.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1091
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1091
- **Title**: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1079` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +1803
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T21:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T00:02:47Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

## Evidence

| AC | Requirement | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC3 | Every cell declared, reasons on ❌/🔀 | `dart test test/hosts/` — 27 tests: completeness over 19×7, blank-reason rejection, transport-vocabulary check, and the 14 matrix rows pinned **cell-exact** (`the 14 matrix rows are pinned cell-exact`) |
| AC4 | Force-enable fails loudly at construction | `iosProfile cannot force-enable mcp over stdio` (both `on` and `transport({'stdio'})` throw `HostProfileViolation` naming profile/capability/floor); manifest-sandbox floors; custom-profile explicit `FloorOff`; floor survives narrowing; macOS `narrow up` to stdio allowed |
| AC10 | Catalog ⊇ every CLI-wired capability, inventory-driven | `every capability-classified inventory item is a catalog row with CLI evidence` (33-item census), rot guard on cited wiring sites, `matrix-floored rows carry no fake CLI evidence` |
| AC7 | Hidden = absent from surfaces | `expectCapabilityHidden` over every hidden cell of all 7 profiles; 🔀 surfaces only chosen transports (`mcp:remote` yes, `mcp:stdio` no on iOS); positive controls; real-text absence on `cliHelpText` |
| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.
- Purity: no `dart:io`/`dart:isolate` imports in `lib/src/hosts/` (grep-verified; doc-comment mentions only).
- Existing suites untouched and green in the worktree: `test/parity/` 32 passed, `test/tools/availability_test.dart` + `test/parity/provider_wiring_guard_test.dart` 47 passed (the capability-floor embryo this card generalizes).
- New: 27/27 tests pass (`dart test test/hosts/`).
- No new dependencies; `pubspec.yaml` untouched.

## Out of scope (slice 2+)

CLI/app shell migration through the builder (AC1), config-parity-through-builder (AC2/AC5), live schema/prompt emission (AC7 IT-4), `HostExtensionApi` + core-invariant negative API (AC9), REG-1 re-run on migrated hosts (AC6), byte-identical CLI behavior proof (AC6). **CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it.**

+/// Declarative per-platform capability profiles (issue #1079, slice 1 —
+/// SDK foundation, additive).
+///
+/// A [HostCapabilityProfile] is the per-platform half of the capability ×
+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's
+/// ceiling — and every state is validated against it at construction.
+/// Violations throw [HostProfileViolation] loudly at build time (AC4), not
+/// at runtime.
+///
+/// Slice 1 ships the record types, the validation, the transport
+/// vocabularies and the seven built-in profiles (in `host_wiring_builder.dart`).
+/// No host migrates to them yet: hosts keep their hand-rolled wiring until
+/// the builder slices land.
+///
+/// Pure Dart: no `dart:io`.

+
+import '../exceptions.dart';

+/// A host-wiring capability: one row of the issue #1079 capability ×
+/// platform matrix.
+///
+/// The set is closed on purpose (E2): adding a value breaks the
+/// matrix-completeness contract until every built-in profile declares it —
+/// "CLI got X, app didn't" dies at compile+construct time, not in a sweep.

+  configSections,
+
+  /// Compaction wiring: roles.smol judge, `overWindowRelief`,
+  /// `contextWindowCap`.
+  compaction,
+

+  loadModes,
+
+  /// MCP servers.
+  mcp,
+
+  /// Messaging fabric transports (file / hub / A2A).
+  messagingFabric,
+
+  /// Approval gate (modes, unattended, always-allow).
+  approvalGate,
+
+  /// Skills + project context.
+  skills,
+
+  /// Sandbox env (cube / platform / WasiSandbox / MemoryShell).
+  sandboxEnv,
+
+  /// Background shell jobs (the `bash_job` board).
+  backgroundShellJobs,
+
+  /// sqlite reader, `lsp`, `dap` tool families.
+  sqliteLspDap,
+
+  /// On-device providers (webllm / gemma in-process inference).
+  onDeviceProviders,
+
+  /// JS apps (jsr) + `dynamic_message` — the browser-API surface.
+  jsApps,
+
+  /// Checkpoint / rewind.
+  checkpointRewind,

+  hostExtensionApi,

+  subagents,

+  /// (`browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, …). Distinct from [jsApps]:
+  /// this is the automation surface the CLI wires today (fah.dart:2143).
+  /// Beyond the issue matrix — inventory-driven (AC10).

messages.preview: The suite is red: **1 of 27 tests fails** despite the PR claiming 27/27 green. Let me investigate the failure root cause and check related surfaces.

blocks.text:
So the `jsr` pass-through was merged into main (#1062), and this PR branch merged main in commit 850e525d1, bringing the `jsr` help text in. The author then re-ran tests... or maybe not. The test now fails because:

1. The `jsApps` capability surface tokens are `{'jsr', 'dynamic_message'}`.
2. The real CLI help legitimately contains `jsr` — as the pass-through delegate for the widget-test CLI (a distinct feature, arguably closest to `jsExtensions`, which is *wired* on the CLI).

The failure is a genuine design flaw in the raw-text absence check: substring matching on short ambiguous tokens (`jsr`) produces false positives when the same string belongs to another, wired capability's surface. The fix is either:
- Disambiguate tokens (e.g. use `/jsr apps` or distinctive tokens), or
- Attribute the `jsr` help section to the right capability (jsExtensions?) — but note `jsExtensions` surface tokens are `{'js_ext', 'jsr.ext'}`, weird tokens, and `jsr.ext` is a weird token (with a dot). Actually `jsr.ext` — hmm.

Also interesting: the PR description explicitly claims "27/27 tests pass (`dart test/hosts/`)" and "the real cliHelpText carries zero jsr/dynamic_message references" — that claim is now false after the main merge. That's a BLOCKING CI issue (the test suite is red).

Note the PR says "CI: not dispatched — owner's SM schedules it" — so the author didn't run CI; the branch is red and the PR description's evidence table is stale/wrong.

Let me also double-check the count of tests: "27 tests" claimed; actual run: 26 passed + 1 failed = 27 total. OK.

Now let me run a broader analysis to look for other issues. Let me check:

1. `dart analyze` on whole repo? Not needed; the changed files are clean.
2. Test the purity claim: no dart:io imports in lib/src/hosts/. The test file imports `dart:io` (fine, it's a test).
3. Look at the naming/structure conventions of the codebase: how other libs are structured, whether enums with switch-based `id` getters match conventions, etc.

Let me also review deeper issues:

**In host_capability_profile.dart:**

1. `HostCapability` enum `id` getter — uses switch expression; fine, but a double space after `jsExtensions;` before the doc comment `/// Stable catalog id`. Minor formatting: there's an extra blank line (two blank lines) between the enum values and the `id` getter. Actually looking at the code:

```dart
  jsExtensions;


  /// Stable catalog id (snake_case, matches the matrix row).
  String get id => switch (this) {
```

There are two blank lines after `jsExtensions;` — dart format would collapse this? Actually `dart format` preserves at most one blank line. So the file is NOT formatted with `dart format` (which is likely enforced by CI or conventional in the repo). Let me check formatting with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none`.

2. In `_validateState`, the message for unknown transports: `'${unknown.isEmpty ? state.transports : unknown}'` — when transports is empty (isEmpty case), it prints `state.transports` which is empty set `{}`. OK-ish. But message reads "unknown transports {} — valid: [...]" which is a bit confusing for the empty case. Minor.

3. `CapabilityState.transport` static method — the constructor `CapabilityTransportState(transports, reason)` — fine.

4. In `HostCapabilityProfile.narrowed`, the merged map uses `Map.of(states)..addAll(overrides)` then `_validate(name: label, states: merged, floors: floors)` and `HostCapabilityProfile._(label, Map.unmodifiable(merged), floors)`. Wait — floors passed to the private constructor is the same map instance as `this.floors`. That's fine since both are unmodifiable.

However, there's a subtle design flaw: `narrowed` does NOT complete the floor table from the new merged states — it keeps the base floors fixed (which is intended per docs). But what if the base profile derived floors from its own states (profile = its own ceiling)? E.g., `narrowed()` on a built-in profile whose floors were derived: the floor table for capabilities not explicitly floored = derived from the ORIGINAL state. So if the original state was `off` and you `narrowed` to `on`, validation checks against `FloorOff` → throws. That's the "profile is its own ceiling" semantics — intended.

But there's a subtle bug: `FloorOff(reason)` from a derived floor — the floor's reason is the ORIGINAL profile's off reason. If you narrow `jsApps: off("x")` on cli (floor derived FloorOff("no browser APIs on the Dart VM...")), fine.

Another subtlety: in `narrowed`, the merged states get validated against the FIXED floor table. But for capabilities whose floors were DERIVED from base states, narrowing a capability to a state whose envelope differs from the base (e.g., base was `transport({'remote'})` → floor `FloorTransports({'remote'})`; narrow to `transport({'remote'})` with different reason) — allowed. Narrow UP to `on` — rejected since defaults {stdio, remote} ⊄ {'remote'}. OK, consistent with "narrow-only".

BUT: the test `macOS may explicitly narrow UP to stdio` works because macos explicitly declares `floors: {mcp: FloorTransports({'stdio', 'remote'})}`. Fine.

5. `CapabilityFloor.fromState(CapabilityOnState() ) => const FloorOn()` — derived floors mean a profile's `on` state allows any state to be narrowed... fine.

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

| AC8 | Capability rules in AGENTS.md | paragraph in "Cross-platform parity": matrix at birth, hide-if-off, narrow-only |

## No-regression proof (pure addition)

- `dart analyze lib/src/hosts test/hosts lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — clean.

+/// platform matrix: for every [HostCapability] it declares ONE state —
+///
+/// - [CapabilityOnState] (`on`) — wired with the SDK's default transports;
+/// - [CapabilityOffState] (`off(reason)`) — not wired; the reason is the
+///   user-visible "why not" (it must surface in UI and prompts, never
+///   silently);
+/// - [CapabilityTransportState] (`transport(choice, reason)`) — wired, but
+///   narrowed to specific transports/stores (the matrix's 🔀 cells).
+///
+/// The **narrowing invariant** (the tool-registry capability floor of
+/// `resolveToolAvailability`, generalized to all host wiring): a profile
+/// can only NARROW what its platform allows, never force-enable what the
+/// platform lacks. Each capability has a [CapabilityFloor] — the platform's

# pr-1091: feat(#1079): SDK slice 1 — HostCapabilityProfile + HostWiringBuilder foundation

## Description

Part of #1079 — **slice 1 of the structural card: the SDK foundation only.** Slices 2+ (CLI/app shell migration, #1077/#1078-through-builder, live emission, HostExtensionApi) are explicitly OUT of this PR; nothing existing migrates and no behavior changes.

## What lands

- **`HostCapabilityProfile`** (`lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`, pure Dart): declarative per-platform record — per capability `on` / `off(reason)` / `transport(choice, reason)`. Every state is validated against the platform **floor** at construction: force-enabling a floored capability throws `HostProfileViolation` loudly (AC4). Profiles can only narrow; `narrowed()` keeps the floor table fixed.
- **Seven built-in profiles** (`host_wiring_builder.dart`): the issue matrix pinned **cell-exact** (14 rows × 7 hosts), every ❌/🔀 cell carrying its reason. Custom hosts construct complete profiles of their own.
- **`HostWiringBuilder` skeleton**: consumes profile + platform services (E1: missing services fail at build, named), exposes the **capability catalog** (union of what the CLI wires today) and returns a typed `HostWiringPlan` — a wiring *description*, not a live stack (slice 2 turns it into the Agent wiring).
- **AC7 hiding helper** (`test/hosts/host_hiding.dart`): reusable assertions — plan-level absence, transport-exact surfacing, and raw-text string-absence — demonstrated on the pinned example: the CLI plan hides `js_apps`, and the **real** `cliHelpText` carries zero `jsr`/`dynamic_message` references.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability-rules paragraph (matrix declaration at birth, hide-if-off in UI + prompts) — AC8 doc half.

## Inventory-driven additions beyond the matrix (AC10)

The verified CLI-wiring sweep (read-only scout, file:line-checked against `bin/fah.dart:2041-2299` + `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:269-769`) found five CLI-wired capabilities **no matrix row covers**: `web_search`/`web_fetch`, vision+transcribe, subagents/task system, the browser tool family (bridge handle), and the QuickJS JS-extension host (distinct from the matrix's browser-API `js_apps` row). They enter the catalog as rows with honest today-states (CLI `on`, other hosts `off("not wired … yet")`), because without them the SDK ⊇ CLI ceiling would be false on arrival. The remaining sweep items classify as core invariants (memory, JSONL session, trajectory — AC9's own list), host glue (TUI, presence, power, secure store, prompt dirs) or config consumers (roles resolver, providers queue, models, custom providers, spills) — the inventory census lives in the AC10 test.

Wait — there's a subtle BUG potential in this regex: the trailing lookahead is actually a consuming character class `[^A-Za-z0-9_]`, not a lookahead. Two consequences:

1. **Adjacent-token misses (false negatives)**: if two occurrences overlap sharing a delimiter, e.g. text "task task" — first match consumes "task " (including the trailing space), and the second "task" starts right after — `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` before it is the space — consumed by previous match? No — regex hasMatch finds the FIRST match anywhere; for ABSENCE checking we only need to know if ANY occurrence exists. Overlapping-consumption only matters with overlapping occurrences like "task"? Not a real concern for hasMatch absence.

   But a REAL false-negative case: two tokens adjacent like "task,lsp" — irrelevant, absence checks are per-token.

   More relevant false-negative: token at text edge handled via `(?:^|...)`. OK.

2. **`dynamic_message` token check on cliHelpText**: pattern `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])dynamic_message(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — help text has no dynamic_message. OK.

So the regex is `(?:$|[^A-Za-z0-9_])` — correct: end of text or non-identifier char. Good.
